title: Framing ML problems and business objectives
description: Business versus ML metrics, classification versus regression framings, multi-objective problems and why to decouple objectives.

title: Requirements of ML systems
description: Reliability, scalability, maintainability and adaptability; latency as a distribution and percentile requirements; the iterative project cycle.

title: Sampling for training data
description: Non-probability versus random sampling, stratified sampling, importance weighting and reservoir sampling on streams.

title: Labelling, weak supervision and data augmentation
description: Natural labels, hand labels, labelling functions and vote aggregation, semi-supervision, active learning and augmentation; data formats and batch versus stream processing.

title: Feature pipelines and feature stores
description: Learned versus engineered features, scaling and encoding with training statistics, feature stores and shared transformation code.

title: Train/serve skew and leakage in systems
description: Leakage patterns in pipelines (time splits, statistics from the test split, duplicates) and automated checks for disagreement between training and serving features.

title: Model selection and offline evaluation
description: Baselines, ensembles, experiment tracking and versioning, distributed training, perturbation, invariance and directional expectation tests.

title: Slice-based evaluation
description: Per-slice metrics, Simpson's paradox, finding critical slices and why an aggregate metric hides failures.

title: Batch and online prediction services
description: Batch versus online prediction, cloud versus edge, deployment myths, and the latency/throughput trade-off of batching requests.

title: Queueing and latency under load
description: Single-server queues, utilisation, tail latency and dynamic batching, simulated with Lindley's recursion and compared with the M/M/1 formula.

title: Model compression for serving
description: Quantisation, knowledge distillation, pruning and low-rank factorisation as ways to cut inference cost.

title: Data distribution shift and its detection
description: Covariate, label and concept shift; software versus ML failures; two-sample tests (KS) and the population stability index.

title: Monitoring and observability for ML
description: Operational versus ML metrics, monitoring features, predictions and accuracy, instrumentation, and alerting thresholds.

title: Continual learning
description: Stateless retraining versus stateful training, why and how often to update models, and the staged path to continual learning.

title: Testing in production: A/B tests, interleaving and bandits
description: Shadow deployment, canary release, A/B testing with a z test, the peeking problem and multi-armed bandits such as Thompson sampling.
